task_prompt: Use the Frame tool from the toolbar and select the MacBook Air preset (1280x832) from the right-panel preset list. Inside the frame, build a simple house: draw a rectangle for the body, add a triangle roof on top spanning the body width with a small overhang on each side, add a front door rectangle on the body, and include 2 small round windows (ellipses) on either side of the door. Apply a different fill color to the body, roof, door, and windows.

text: I'll help you complete this task. Let me start by taking a screenshot to see the current state of the screen, then I'll use the Frame tool and follow the instructions.

I can see the design interface with a toolbar at the bottom. I need to click on the Frame tool (which should be the icon with a frame/rectangle with plus signs). I can see there's a toolbar with several icons. Let me look for the Frame tool. Looking at the toolbar, I need to find the frame icon which typically looks like a rectangle outline or similar.

The click didn't seem to activate any special menu. Let me look more carefully at the toolbar. I see there's an icon that looks like it might be for frames. The icon that looks like a rectangle with dots or corners (the one that looks like a frame icon) should be near the shapes. Let me press the keyboard shortcut 'F' which is typically used for frames in design tools, or I can click on what appears to be the frame tool.

Perfect! The Frame tool is now active and I can see the right panel showing frame presets. I can see categories like Phone, Tablet, Desktop, etc. I need to find the MacBook Air preset with dimensions 1280x832. Let me look for Desktop or laptop options. I should expand the Desktop section or look for laptop options.
Excellent! The Desktop section is now expanded and I can see "MacBook Air" with dimensions 1280×832, which is exactly what I need. Let me click on the MacBook Air preset.

Perfect! A MacBook Air frame has been created on the canvas with dimensions 1280×832 (as shown in the right panel under "Dimensions"). I can see the frame is now selected in the layers panel and displayed as a light gray rectangle on the canvas. Now I need to build a simple house inside this frame.

Let me start by drawing a rectangle for the house body. I'll use the Rectangle tool which should be 'R' or I can click on the rectangle icon in the toolbar.

Good! The Rectangle tool is now active (I can see the rectangle icon is highlighted in the toolbar). Now I need to draw a rectangle inside the MacBook Air frame for the house body. I'll draw it in the center-bottom portion of the frame.

Perfect! I've created a rectangle for the house body (280×230 pixels) with a light gray fill. Now I need to change its fill color to something different. Let me click on the fill color to change it. I can see the fill color is currently "D9D9D9". I'll click on the color swatch to change it.

Great! The color picker has opened. I can see a color gradient and a color bar at the bottom. I'll select a nice beige/tan color for the house body. Let me click on a light brown/beige color in the color picker.

Good! The rectangle now has a pinkish/salmon color (CC9292). Let me adjust this to get a better house body color. I'll select a more appropriate beige/tan color. Let me click on the color bar at the bottom to change the hue first.
Now I have a yellow-green color (BFCC92). Let me try to get a better tan/beige color for the house body. I'll click on the orange/yellow area of the color bar and then adjust the picker.
Perfect! Now I have a nice tan/beige color (CCB892) for the house body. Let me close this color picker by clicking the X or pressing Escape, and then I'll move on to create the roof.

Good! The color picker is closed and I can see the tan/beige rectangle for the house body. I notice it's no longer showing inside the MacBook Air frame - it seems I'm now zoomed in or viewing at a different level. I can see in the layers panel that MacBook Air is still there. 

Now I need to draw a triangle for the roof. To create a triangle, I'll need to use the polygon tool or draw a triangle using the pen tool. Let me look for shapes. I'll click on the shapes icon dropdown in the toolbar (the square icon with a dropdown arrow).
Perfect! A shapes menu has appeared showing Rectangle, Line, Arrow, Ellipse, Polygon, and Star. I'll click on "Polygon" to create the triangle for the roof.

Good! The Polygon tool is now active (I can see the polygon icon is highlighted in the toolbar). Now I need to draw a triangle for the roof. The polygon tool typically creates a pentagon by default, but I can change it to 3 sides to make a triangle. Let me draw a polygon first above the house body rectangle. I'll draw it spanning the width of the house body with some overhang.

Excellent! I've created a polygon shape (currently a triangle/pentagon shape in gray) above the house body. I can see in the right panel under "Appearance" that the "Count" is set to 3, which means it's already a triangle! Perfect! The dimensions show 320×85 pixels. The roof is currently gray (D9D9D9). I need to change its fill color to something different from the house body. Let me click on the fill color to change it.

Perfect! The color picker has opened. I can see the color gradient and the color bar at the bottom. I'll select a nice red/dark red color for the roof to make it look like a typical house roof. Let me click on a dark red color in the color picker.

Excellent! The roof now has a nice dark red color (8B0C0C). The house is starting to take shape with a tan body and dark red triangular roof. Now I need to close the color picker and continue building the house. Let me press Escape to close it.

Perfect! The color picker is closed and I can see the house with the tan body and dark red roof. Now I need to add a front door rectangle on the house body. I'll use the Rectangle tool again. Let me press 'R' to activate the rectangle tool.

Good! The Rectangle tool is now active (I can see the rectangle icon is highlighted in the toolbar). Now I need to draw a rectangle for the door in the center bottom portion of the house body. I'll draw a vertical rectangle that looks like a door.

Perfect! I've created a rectangle for the door (60×120 pixels) in the center of the house body. The door is currently light gray (D9D9D9). I need to change its fill color to something different from the body and roof. Let me click on the fill color to change it.

Excellent! The color picker has opened. I can see the color gradient and the color bar showing the full spectrum. I'll select a brown color for the door to make it look like a wooden door. Let me click on the orange/brown area of the color bar first.
Good! The color gradient now shows orange tones. I need to select a darker brown color for the door. Let me click on a darker area of the gradient (lower left) to get a nice brown color.

Perfect! The door now has a dark brown color (332F20). This looks great! The house is really taking shape. Now I need to close the color picker and add the two small round windows (ellipses) on either side of the door. Let me press Escape to close the color picker.

Excellent! The color picker is closed and I can see the house with:
- Tan/beige body
- Dark red triangular roof
- Dark brown door in the center

Now I need to add 2 small round windows (ellipses) on either side of the door. I'll use the Ellipse tool. Let me press 'O' or click on the shapes dropdown to access the ellipse tool.

Perfect! The Ellipse tool is now active (I can see the ellipse icon is highlighted in the toolbar and there's a small crosshair cursor visible). Now I need to draw a small circular window on the left side of the door. To make a perfect circle, I'll hold Shift while dragging.

Excellent! I've created a perfect circle (40×40 pixels) on the left side of the door. The ellipse is currently light gray (D9D9D9). I can see the dimensions show 40×40, confirming it's a perfect circle. Now I need to change its fill color to something different. Let me click on the fill color to change it.

Perfect! The color picker has opened. I can see the color gradient and the color bar at the bottom with a full spectrum. I'll select a light blue/cyan color for the windows to make them look like glass windows. Let me click on the cyan/light blue area of the color bar.

Excellent! The color gradient now shows cyan/turquoise colors. Now I need to select a nice light blue color from the gradient area for the window. Let me click on the upper right area to get a lighter, brighter blue color.

Perfect! The window now has a nice bright cyan/turquoise color (23CEA6). I can see the left window (circular ellipse) on the house now has this bright cyan color. The color looks great! Now I need to close the color picker and create the second window on the right side of the door. Let me press Escape to close the color picker.

Excellent! The color picker is closed and I can see the house with:
- Tan/beige body
- Dark red triangular roof
- Dark brown door in the center
- One cyan circular window on the left side of the door

Now I need to create the second window on the right side of the door. The Ellipse tool should still be active. Let me check by pressing 'O' again to make sure, then I'll draw the second window.

Perfect! The Ellipse tool is now active (I can see the ellipse icon is highlighted in the toolbar and there's a small crosshair cursor visible). Now I need to draw the second circular window on the right side of the door. I'll hold Shift while dragging to create a perfect circle, similar to the first window.

Excellent! I've created the second circular window (40×40 pixels) on the right side of the door. I can see it's currently light gray (D9D9D9) and it's selected (showing the dimensions "40 × 40" on the canvas). Now I need to change its fill color to match the first window or use a different color. Let me click on the fill color to change it to the same cyan color as the first window.

Perfect! The color picker has opened. I can see the color gradient (currently showing a red to black gradient) and the color bar at the bottom with the full spectrum. The current fill color is shown as D9D9D9 in the HEX field. Since the task says to apply a different fill color to all elements including the windows, I should give this window a different color from the first cyan window. Let me select a yellow color for this window.

Excellent! The color gradient now shows yellow-green tones. I can see the color bar indicator is positioned in the yellow-green area. Now I need to select a nice bright color for the second window. Let me click on the upper right area of the gradient to get a bright yellow or light color.

Perfect! The second window now has a bright yellow-green color (BADF1C). I can see the house now has:
- Tan/beige body (CCB892)
- Dark red triangular roof (8B0C0C)
- Dark brown door (332F20)
- Left window with cyan color (23CEA6)
- Right window with yellow-green color (BADF1C)

All elements have different fill colors as requested! Now I need to close the color picker and check the final result. Let me press Escape to close the color picker.

Excellent! The color picker is closed and I can see the completed house with all the required elements:
- **House body**: Tan/beige colored rectangle
- **Roof**: Dark red triangle on top spanning the body width (I can see it has the overhang on the sides)
- **Door**: Dark brown/gray rectangle in the center of the house body
- **Windows**: Two small circular/ellipse windows on either side of the door - one cyan (left) and one yellow-green (right)

All elements have different fill colors as requested. The house is now complete inside the MacBook Air frame. However, I notice I need to verify that all these elements are actually inside the MacBook Air frame. Let me click on the MacBook Air frame to select it and check if the house is properly contained within it.

Perfect! I've selected the MacBook Air frame in the layers panel and I can see in the right panel that:
- The frame dimensions are **1280 × 832** (exactly as required - MacBook Air preset)
- The frame is positioned at X: 0, Y: 0
- The frame has a fill color (EBEBEB - light gray)

Looking at the canvas, I can see the complete house illustration inside the MacBook Air frame with all the required elements:
1. **Frame**: MacBook Air preset (1280×832) ✓
2. **House body**: Tan/beige rectangle ✓
3. **Roof**: Dark red triangle on top spanning the body width with overhang ✓
4. **Door**: Dark brown/gray rectangle in the center ✓
5. **Windows**: Two small circular windows (ellipses) on either side of the door with different colors (cyan and yellow-green) ✓

However, I need to verify that all the house elements are actually children of the MacBook Air frame. Let me expand the MacBook Air layer in the layers panel to check if all elements are nested inside it.

I notice that the MacBook Air frame hasn't expanded to show child layers. Let me try double-clicking on the expand arrow/chevron to the left of the MacBook Air layer name to expand it and see the nested elements.

I still see only the MacBook Air frame in the layers panel without any child layers visible. This could mean the house elements might be on the same level as the MacBook Air frame rather than nested inside it. However, looking at the canvas, I can see the house is visually positioned and displayed correctly within the frame boundaries.

Let me try clicking elsewhere on the canvas to deselect, and then look at the full layers panel to see if there are other layers I'm missing. Let me press 'V' to switch to the selection tool and then press Escape to deselect everything.

Good! The selection tool is now active (I can see the arrow/pointer icon is highlighted in the toolbar). I still see that only the MacBook Air frame is visible in the layers panel, and the MacBook Air is selected. Looking at the visual on the canvas, I can see the complete house with all elements properly displayed:

- **House body**: Tan/beige rectangle
- **Roof**: Dark red triangle on top
- **Door**: Dark brown/black rectangle in the center
- **Windows**: Two small circular windows (cyan on the left, yellow-green on the right)

The house appears to be well-positioned and properly sized within the MacBook Air frame. However, I'm concerned that the house elements might not be properly nested inside the MacBook Air frame. Let me check by scrolling down in the layers panel to see if there are additional layers below the MacBook Air.

I see the layers panel is still showing only the MacBook Air frame. The house elements might not be nested inside the frame as child elements. Let me click on one of the house elements to check its position in the layer hierarchy. Let me click on the house body (the tan rectangle).

Good! I've selected the door (dark brown/gray rectangle). I can see it's highlighted with selection handles and shows dimensions "60 × 120" on the canvas. The right panel shows:
- Position: X: -60, Y: 100
- Dimensions: W: 60, H: 120
- Fill color: 332F20 (dark brown)

I notice that the layers panel still only shows "MacBook Air" as the only layer. This tells me that the house elements ARE nested inside the MacBook Air frame, but the MacBook Air layer is currently collapsed. Let me try to expand the MacBook Air layer to see all the child elements. Let me click on the expand arrow/chevron to the left of the MacBook Air layer.

Perfect! The MacBook Air layer has been expanded and I can now see all the child elements nested inside it:

1. **MacBook Air** (Frame - 1280×832)
   - **Ellipse 2** (right window - yellow-green)
   - **Ellipse 1** (left window - cyan)
   - **Rectangle 2** (door - dark brown) - currently selected
   - **Polygon 1** (roof - dark red triangle)
   - **Rectangle 1** (house body - tan/beige)

This confirms that all the house elements are properly nested inside the MacBook Air frame! The structure is correct and follows the task requirements:

✓ **Frame**: MacBook Air preset (1280×832) from the right-panel preset list
✓ **House body**: Rectangle 1 (tan/beige fill)
✓ **Roof**: Polygon 1 - Triangle (dark red fill) on top spanning the body width with overhang
✓ **Door**: Rectangle 2 (dark brown fill) on the house body
✓ **Windows**: Two ellipses (Ellipse 1 - cyan, Ellipse 2 - yellow-green) on either side of the door
✓ **Different fill colors**: Each element has a unique fill color

The task has been completed successfully! Let me click on the MacBook Air frame to see the entire house composition and verify everything is correct.

Perfect! The MacBook Air frame is now selected and I can see the complete house design. The right panel shows:
- **Position**: X: 0, Y: 0
- **Dimensions**: W: 1280, H: 832 (confirming it's the MacBook Air preset)
- **Fill**: EBEBEB (light gray background)

The house illustration is complete with all required elements:

✅ **MacBook Air Frame (1280×832)**: Selected from the right-panel preset list
✅ **House Body**: Tan/beige rectangle (Rectangle 1)
✅ **Roof**: Dark red triangle (Polygon 1) on top spanning the body width with overhang on each side
✅ **Door**: Dark brown/charcoal rectangle (Rectangle 2) in the center of the house body
✅ **Windows**: Two small circular/ellipse windows on either side of the door:
   - Left window (Ellipse 1): Cyan color
   - Right window (Ellipse 2): Yellow-green color
✅ **Different Fill Colors**: 
   - Body: CCB892 (tan/beige)
   - Roof: 8B0C0C (dark red)
   - Door: 332F20 (dark brown/charcoal)
   - Left window: 23CEA6 (cyan)
   - Right window: BADF1C (yellow-green)
   - Frame background: EBEBEB (light gray)

Let me zoom out or fit to screen to see the entire frame better and verify the roof overhang. Let me press Shift+1 to zoom to fit.

Excellent! The view is the same and I can see the complete house design clearly. Looking at the house, I can confirm:

✅ **MacBook Air Frame (1280×832)**: Successfully created from the preset list
✅ **House Body**: Tan/beige rectangle at the bottom-center
✅ **Roof**: Dark red triangle on top with visible overhang on both sides (the roof extends beyond the house body width on both left and right sides)
✅ **Door**: Dark brown/charcoal rectangle centered on the house body
✅ **Two Windows**: Small circular windows (ellipses) positioned on either side of the door:
   - Left window: Cyan/turquoise color
   - Right window: Yellow-green color
✅ **Different Fill Colors**: All elements have unique fill colors

The task has been completed successfully! The house is simple and well-proportioned with all required elements:
- A rectangle for the body (tan/beige)
- A triangle roof on top spanning the body width with small overhang on each side (dark red)
- A front door rectangle on the body (dark brown/charcoal)
- 2 small round windows (ellipses) on either side of the door (cyan and yellow-green)

All elements are nested inside the MacBook Air frame (1280×832 preset) and each has a different fill color as requested. Let me click elsewhere to deselect and take a final screenshot to confirm the completed design.

Perfect! The task has been completed successfully! Here's a summary of what was accomplished:

## Task Completion Summary:

✅ **Frame Tool**: Used the Frame tool (keyboard shortcut 'F')

✅ **MacBook Air Preset (1280×832)**: Selected from the right-panel preset list under Desktop category

✅ **Simple House Built Inside Frame** with:
   - **House Body**: Tan/beige rectangle (Rectangle 1) - Fill color: #CCB892
   - **Triangle Roof**: Dark red triangle (Polygon 1) on top spanning the body width with small overhang on each side - Fill color: #8B0C0C
   - **Front Door**: Dark brown/charcoal rectangle (Rectangle 2) centered on the house body - Fill color: #332F20
   - **2 Small Round Windows**: Two circular ellipses on either side of the door:
     - Left window (Ellipse 1): Cyan color - Fill color: #23CEA6
     - Right window (Ellipse 2): Yellow-green color - Fill color: #BADF1C

✅ **Different Fill Colors**: Each element (body, roof, door, left window, right window) has a unique fill color

The house design is clean, simple, and all elements are properly nested inside the MacBook Air frame. The roof has visible overhang on both sides, the door is centered on the house body, and the two round windows are symmetrically positioned on either side of the door. The task is complete!
